claims.text: The driver's own trace shows he held position inside the pickup geofence for only 67 continuous seconds, from 12:51:17 to 12:52:24, before he cancelled at 12:52:28. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec). The effective in-geofence dwell is therefore 113 seconds short of the minimum, and under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is not chargeable and must be refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.

The shortfall is confirmed on the face of the trip record itself: the platform's own wait timer started at 12:51:19 and the driver cancelled at 12:52:28, a recorded wait of 1.2 minutes against a 180 second free waiting period. The driver terminated the trip before the waiting period he was required to give had elapsed.

The rider was at the pickup and actively coordinating. At 12:52:17 she messaged 'im at the lobby, coming out', and the driver's only reply, 'ok', was sent at 12:52:32 - after he had already cancelled at 12:52:28. The rider's own track places her device within 13 to 19 metres of the pickup pin throughout, well inside the 100 m rider presence radius for a STANDARD zone, across 39 qualifying fixes. The driver cancelled without ever answering her locating message.

The driver's stated reason for cancelling - 'Rider was not visible and I had another booking waiting' - is his own admission that he left the pickup to take another job. A driver who abandons the pickup before the free waiting period has elapsed cannot convert his own departure into a rider no-show charge.

The fare ledger shows the rider was charged SGD 4.50 with no refund issued (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). That is the amount the rider contests and the amount that must be returned to her.

No traffic advisory covers this pickup road in this window - the advisory artifact is MISSING and carries weight 0.0. Under POL-NS-06(i) a MISSING traffic_advisory makes the accumulation limb unavailable, so the driver cannot add any separate in-geofence interval to his 67 seconds, and the shortfall stands.

The rider's profile shows no_show_disputes_30d of 0 and no disputes with this counterparty in the trailing 90 days, so nothing in the record supports treating this as abuse by the rider; the escalation trigger in POL-NS-09(d) is not met on her side.

claims.text: The driver's own GPS trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for a continuous qualifying run of 67 seconds, from 12:51:17 to 12:52:24, with 8 qualifying fixes — but the free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), so the dwell falls 113 seconds short of the minimum. POL-NS-01 limb (c) therefore fails and the fee is not chargeable under that clause.

The shortfall is arithmetic and undisputed on the driver's own evidence: the required minimum dwell for a STANDARD pickup is 180 seconds, the measured effective in-geofence dwell is 67 seconds, and the shortfall is 113 seconds. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.

The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 12:51:17 and the platform's own wait timer started at 12:51:19 with a free waiting period of 180 seconds, yet the driver cancelled at 12:52:28 — 69 seconds after the timer started, and 113 seconds before the free waiting period he was obliged to give had elapsed. The trip record's own event chain confirms the premature termination.

The rider was present and coordinating: the rider's track shows 39 fixes, all within a maximum of 19.08 m of the pickup pin, well inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, and the rider messaged 'im at the lobby, coming out' at 12:52:17 — 11 seconds before the driver cancelled. The rider was at the pickup point and actively trying to complete the pickup when the driver terminated the trip.

The driver's reply 'ok' was sent at 12:52:32, four seconds AFTER he had already cancelled the trip at 12:52:28. The driver terminated the trip before answering the rider's locating message, and no in-app voice call is recorded in trip_record.in_app_calls. Under POL-NS-04 limbs (a) and (b) the rider is exonerated and the fee is refunded in full with no driver compensation payable.

The fare breakdown shows the cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 was charged to the rider at 12:52:45 with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The amount contested is SGD 4.50, and the full refund of that cancellation-fee line is what POL-NS-06 directs.

The driver's own counterparty statement — 'Rider was not visible and I had another booking waiting' — is an admission that he left the pickup to take another job rather than serving out the free waiting period. A driver who departs for another booking has not held position for the required dwell, and POL-NS-01 limb (c) is not satisfied on his own account of events.

The traffic advisory artifact for this pickup is MISSING — no advisory covers Blk 108 Yishun Ring Rd in this window — so POL-NS-06 limb (i) is unavailable and the driver cannot accumulate dwell across separate in-geofence intervals or excuse the shortfall on grounds of a kerb restriction, enforcement operation, closure or accident. The absence itself is citable and it removes the driver's only counter to the shortfall.

The rider's profile shows no_show_disputes_30d of 0 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0, and the driver's profile shows disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0, so neither POL-NS-09(c) nor POL-NS-09(d) is engaged and there is no repeat-abuse pattern that would send this case to human review instead of a refund. The rider's prior_no_show_flags of 0 is a lifetime counter and is not the field POL-NS-09(d) reads.

The GPS trace is clean and unimpaired: 100.0% coverage, 51 fixes at a 10 second cadence, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, and both driver and rider tracks present, with admissibility weight 1.0. The shortfall finding rests on evidence at full weight, so the confidence cap under POL-GEN-02(2) does not push this case below the 0.70 escalation floor and no escalation under POL-NS-09(a) is required.

The driver's profile shows no_show_terminations_30d of 0 against completed_trips_30d of 107, so the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip and there is no basis to withhold compensation or escalate under POL-NS-09(d). That is a concession that the driver is not a fee-farmer — but it does not help him here, because POL-NS-07 compensation is only payable where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not.

The rider filed this dispute, so NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03 would leave the SGD 4.50 charge standing against the rider and the refund at 0.00 — that is not a neutral outcome, it is a loss for the rider on a fee the driver's own trace shows was collected 113 seconds early. The correct ruling on these facts is FULL_REFUND of the cancellation fee.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02706 is refunded in full to the rider.

The driver's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-02706) is the deciding evidence. It shows he held position inside the 50 m STANDARD pickup geofence for a longest continuous qualifying run of 67 seconds, from 12:51:17 to 12:52:24 — 113 seconds short of the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, read from EV-TRIP-02706). The trip record says the same from its own side: the platform wait timer started at 12:51:19 and the driver cancelled at 12:52:28, 69 seconds later. POL-NS-01 limb (c) requires a continuous dwell of at least the free waiting period, so it fails, and POL-NS-06 directs that the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02706) shows SGD 4.50 charged with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00; that SGD 4.50 is the amount returned.

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 compensates the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not. The driver's profile shows no_show_terminations_30d of 0 against completed_trips_30d of 107, so the anti-farming check is not in issue either way; there is simply no satisfied POL-NS-01 for compensation to attach to.

On the rider's POL-NS-04 claim: the rider's track within EV-GPS-02706 places her device within about 19 m of the pin across 39 fixes, and she messaged 'im at the lobby, coming out' at 12:52:17, 11 seconds before the driver cancelled; the driver's 'ok' came at 12:52:32, after the cancellation, and no in-app call is recorded. That account is consistent with the outcome but is not needed for it — POL-NS-06 gives the refund regardless of rider presence.

On the driver's statement that the rider was not visible and he had another booking waiting: that account cannot carry a no-show fee here. A driver who leaves to take another booking has not served the waiting period POL-NS-01(c) requires, and his own trace confirms he cancelled 113 seconds early. The RIDER_NO_SHOW reason code was correctly chosen on its face, so no reason-code referral arises.

On confidence (POL-GEN-02): every artifact carrying the deciding fact — EV-GPS-02706 and EV-TRIP-02706 — is at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and the finding does not approach the 0.70 floor. The MISSING traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02706-01, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no deciding fact: it only makes the POL-NS-06(i) accumulation limb unavailable, which does not change the shortfall, so it does not lower the cap. No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is met — confidence is above the floor, the citable profile counters (rider no_show_disputes_30d 0; both disputes_with_counterparty_90d 0) show no repeat abuse, and no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence. The monetary effect of SGD 4.50 is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00. The arrival marker was not false (the first qualifying in-geofence fix coincides with the 12:51:17 arrival tap), so no POL-NS-05 false-arrival referral is made.

Two claims — one from each advocate, both about the missing traffic advisory — were discarded at the citation stage because they cited the weight-0.0 artifact EV-ADVIS-02706-01 without naming its MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code; they are recorded in discarded_claims.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides' evidence agrees on what decides this case, so the outcome is the same however the parties frame it.

The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 12:51:17 and the platform started a 180-second free waiting period at 12:51:19 (EV-TRIP-02706, platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180 s). He cancelled at 12:52:28, and his own GPS trace shows one continuous in-geofence run of 67 seconds, from 12:51:17 to 12:52:24, on 8 qualifying fixes (EV-GPS-02706, derived.arrival.longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec = 67 s; derived.arrival.shortfall_sec = 113 s). The trip record's own wait timer tells the same story: 69 seconds of waiting against 180 seconds required. POL-NS-01 limb (c) therefore fails - the driver did not hold position for the free waiting period in force - and limb (d) fails with it, because the trip was not terminated at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed. The fee was not earned under POL-NS-01.

POL-NS-06 then governs the refund: where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the waiting period in force, the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages. The rider's message 'im at the lobby, coming out' at 12:52:17 and her track (39 fixes within 13-19 m of the pin) are consistent with that but are not needed for it. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02706) shows the SGD 4.50 cancellation-fee line charged at 12:52:45 with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and that is the sum refunded.

The driver cannot top up his dwell by summing separate intervals: under POL-NS-06(i) that route requires a present and populated traffic advisory, and EV-ADVIS-02706-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0), so limb (i) is unavailable and no separate intervals can be added. Two claims on that point were discarded at the mechanical check (a zero-weight artifact was cited without naming the MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code).

On the claim that POL-NS-04 exonerates the rider: it is not needed and does not decide this case. The outcome it would produce - full refund with no driver compensation - is the outcome POL-NS-06 already produces on the dwell arithmetic. I note only that the driver's single chat reply 'ok' was posted at 12:52:32, four seconds after he had already cancelled at 12:52:28.

To the rider and the driver: the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02706 is refunded in full to the rider, and no driver compensation is payable.

The driver did tap 'I'm Here' at 12:51:17 (EV-TRIP-02706) and the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02706) does place him inside the 50 m STANDARD pickup geofence at that moment, so limbs (a) and (b) are met. But the trace shows him holding position inside the geofence for only 67 continuous seconds, from 12:51:17 to 12:52:24, across 8 qualifying fixes. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, EV-TRIP-02706), so the dwell falls 113 seconds short - the shortfall figure EV-GPS-02706 itself reports. The platform's own wait timer started at 12:51:19 and the driver cancelled at 12:52:28, 69 seconds later. POL-NS-01(c) therefore fails, and under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-02706) shows SGD 4.50 charged at 12:52:45 with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00; that is the figure returned.

No driver compensation. POL-NS-07 pays the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not. The anti-farming check does not trip either: EV-DPROF-02706 shows no_show_terminations_30d of 0 against completed_trips_30d of 107.

The arrival marker is not false. At 12:51:17 the driver was already inside the geofence and stationary, so the waiting clock is not recomputed under POL-NS-05 and no false-arrival referral arises.

The driver's statement that 'Rider was not visible and I had another booking waiting' does not save the fee. The charge does not turn on whether the rider was visible; it turns on the driver serving out the waiting period, which the trace shows he did not. For completeness, the rider's own track (EV-GPS-02706) places her device 13-19 m from the pin across 39 fixes, and her message 'im at the lobby, coming out' (EV-CHAT-02706) was sent at 12:52:17, eleven seconds before the driver cancelled at 12:52:28. His 'ok' reply came at 12:52:32, after cancellation; because a reply was posted within 120 seconds of the rider's message, POL-NS-04 limb (b) is not clearly made out, but nothing turns on it - the refund and the nil compensation follow independently from POL-NS-06.

The traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02706-01) is MISSING at weight 0.0 and can carry no fact; POL-NS-06 limb (i) accumulation is therefore unavailable and does not help the driver. The two claims arguing from that artifact were discarded because they did not disclose its issue code.

Profiles were used only where a clause names them: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d (0) and both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d (0) mean neither POL-NS-09(c) nor POL-NS-09(d) is engaged. rider_profile.prior_no_show_flags is a lifetime counter, is context only under POL-GEN-01, and was not used to establish anything.

ruling.explanation:
The cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 charged on TRP-02706 is refunded to the rider in full.

Why the fee does not stand. Under POL-NS-01 the fee is chargeable only if all four conditions hold. Condition (a) holds: the trip record (EV-TRIP-02706) contains a driver 'arrived' event at 12:51:17. Condition (b) holds: the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02706) places the vehicle at the pickup pin, so the arrival marker is genuine — this is not a POL-NS-05 false-arrival case, and because the driver was inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius it is not a POL-NS-03 wrong-entrance case either. Condition (d) is arguable. Condition (c) fails, and that is the whole case. POL-NS-01(c) requires the driver to hold position inside the geofence for a continuous dwell of at least the free waiting period in force — 180 seconds, read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec (EV-TRIP-02706). The driver's own trace shows a single continuous in-geofence run of 67 seconds, from 12:51:17 to 12:52:24, and the platform's own wait timer ran from 12:51:19 to the cancellation at 12:52:28 — about 69 seconds against the required 180. The shortfall is 113 seconds. POL-NS-06 therefore applies directly: the fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages, and no driver compensation is payable.

Both advocates' arithmetic is accepted, because both sides state the same figures from the same artifacts: the required minimum (180 s, from trip_record.platform_policy), the measured dwell (67 s), and the shortfall (113 s). The rider's claim that the fare ledger shows SGD 4.50 charged with refund 0.00 (EV-FARE-02706, payment_status CHARGED) is accepted, and SGD 4.50 is the amount returned. The driver's advocate's submission that NO_ACTION would simply leave the SGD 4.50 charge standing against the rider is accepted; that is not the outcome on these facts.

On POL-NS-04 (rider contact unanswered by driver), the rider's message at 12:52:17 ('im at the lobby, coming out') was a locating message and her device sat within 13–19 m of the pin across 39 fixes (EV-GPS-02706), well inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. But limb (b) is not satisfied: the driver's reply 'ok' was posted at 12:52:32, within 120 seconds of that message, and POL-NS-04 does not apply where the driver replied inside that window. Both advocates' POL-NS-04 arguments are therefore not the ground of the refund — but the refund follows from POL-NS-06 independently, so the outcome is unchanged.

The driver's counterparty statement — 'Rider was not visible and I had another booking waiting' — is his own account. It is evidence, but it does not move the arithmetic: it is not a concession of a refund, and it cannot make a RIDER_NO_SHOW reason code good on a cancellation that occurred before the waiting period had run. A cancelled booking made to take another job is not a served waiting period.

No escalation ground under POL-NS-09 is engaged. Confidence is above the 0.70 floor; the artifacts do not contradict one another on arrival, dwell or rider presence; rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both profiles, so neither limb (c) nor limb (d) fires; and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (driver no_show_terminations_30d = 0 against completed_trips_30d = 107). The profile fields were used only where the policy names them.

On the evidence: the deciding fact — the 67-second dwell against a 180-second minimum — is carried by EV-GPS-02706 and EV-TRIP-02706, each at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and no discount applies. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02706-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, which makes POL-NS-06(i) accumulation unavailable, but it decides nothing here: the trace shows a single in-geofence run, so there are no separate intervals to sum. The monetary effect (SGD 4.50) is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00 and executes on issue. The charge was recorded under the reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW on a cancellation where the fee was not chargeable; the reviewer may wish to note that for driver education.
